hooks.spoken: Miss the last 2 letters and you pay in the wrong currency.

slides.promise:

slides.say: Hama reads the end of the name first.

slides.text: Two funds can track the same index and still hand you a different return. The difference is hiding in the last two characters.
slides.under: Nobody puts it in the headline. It sits at the end of the ticker.
slides.say: Same index. Not the same fund.

slides.title: Dot U
slides.meaning: The same fund, priced and traded in US dollars.
slides.example: Your CAD never converts. You bring USD in yourself.
slides.say: Not a different fund. A different currency.

slides.title: Dot F
slides.meaning: Currency hedged. The CAD–USD swing is stripped out.
slides.example: Invesco Canada moved its hedged funds onto this one.
slides.say: Hedged means the exchange rate is handled for you.

slides.title: Just H
slides.meaning: Also hedged. RBC puts it at the end, with no dot.
slides.example: Same job as .F. Different letter, different issuer.
slides.say: Two letters, one job. Nobody agreed on which.

slides.title: No suffix
slides.meaning: Nothing on the ticker. The hedge is written in the fund's full name.
slides.example: TD writes CAD Hedged into the name instead.
slides.say: So the ticker alone is not enough.

slides.title: The catch
slides.meaning: There is no single rule. Conventions differ from issuer to issuer.
slides.example: So the key below gets you close. The issuer page confirms it.
slides.say: Hama checks the issuer page every time.

rows.m: No standard. Confirm with the issuer

caption:
Skip the last 2 letters and you buy the wrong ETF.

Two funds. Same index. Different money in your pocket.

Here's the key. A .U means the fund is priced in US dollars, so your CAD never converts. A .F means currency hedged, and Invesco Canada moved every hedged fund onto it. RBC uses a plain H, no dot. TD doesn't touch the ticker at all and writes CAD Hedged into the name instead.

4 issuers. 4 habits. No standard.

The key below gets you close. The issuer's own fund page settles it.

Read the last 2 characters before your next buy.
